children: , the enterprise-cybersecurity platform, launched a new subscription service built to hunt for security weaknesses continuously instead of waiting for the next scheduled assessment. Shares fell approximately 1.2% to $367.35.

Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense brings together Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5, OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Cyber and open-weight models to probe applications, APIs and cloud infrastructure for vulnerabilities and potential attack paths. The platform can also recommend code-level fixes and virtual patches, while annual pricing varies depending on the mix of AI models a customer chooses. That gives Palo Alto a way to push more Unit 42 work into an always-on product rather than relying only on periodic consulting engagements.

The economics are where this gets interesting. Recurring contracts could make security testing more predictable and scalable, but heavy model usage can also bring meaningful compute costs, while difficult remediation work may still need human specialists. The valuation picture leaves little room for disappointment: the shares trade at $367.35 versus a GF Value of $233.09, putting the market price 57.6% above GF Value. That gap suggests investors are already pricing in substantial growth, making renewal rates and service margins more important than simply showing how many vulnerabilities the AI can uncover.

title: Palo Alto Falls 1.2% as AI Becomes Its Own Penetration Tester
